Success Criterion 4.1.1 Parsing (Obsolete and removed)
Note
This criterion was originally adopted to address problems that assistive technology had directly parsing HTML. Assistive technology no longer has any need to directly parse HTML. old_spans.quote:
Success Criterion 4.1.1 Parsing
(Level A)
In content implemented using markup languages, elements have complete start and end
tags, elements are nested according to their specifications, elements do not contain
duplicate attributes, and any IDs are unique, except where the specifications allow
these features.
Note
Start and end tags that are missing a critical character in their formation, such
as a closing angle bracket or a mismatched attribute value quotation mark are not
complete.

semantics.reason: In WCAG 2.1 (2018), SC 4.1.1 Parsing is ACTIVE at Level A, requiring complete start/end tags, proper nesting, no duplicate attributes, and unique IDs in markup languages, with a note on incomplete tags. In WCAG 2.2 (2023), the same section ID 'parsing' is present but explicitly marked 'Obsolete and removed'; the source note states assistive technology no longer needs to directly parse HTML, these problems no longer exist or are addressed by other criteria, and the criterion 'no longer has utility and is removed.' This constitutes explicit removal evidence, making the new state OBSOLETE. Implication values are NOT_APPLICABLE because one state is not ACTIVE.

lines: When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.

Where content in a configurable interface can be repositioned by the user, then only the initial positions of user-movable content are considered for testing and conformance of this Success Criterion.

Content opened by the user may obscure the component receiving focus. If the user can reveal the focused component without advancing the keyboard focus, the component with focus is not considered hidden due to author-created content.

new_spans.quote:
Success Criterion 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
(Level AA)
[New]
When a user interface component receives keyboard focus, the component is not entirely hidden due to author-created content.
Note 1
Where content in a configurable interface can be repositioned by the user, then only the initial positions of user-movable content are considered for testing and conformance of this Success Criterion.
Note 2
Content opened by the user may obscure the component receiving focus. If the user can reveal the focused component without advancing the keyboard focus, the component with focus is not considered hidden due to author-created content.

semantics.reason: The old version’s complete section index does not contain section ID "focus-not-obscured-minimum", so the old state is ABSENT. The new version contains that section and states an AA requirement: when a UI component receives keyboard focus, it must not be entirely hidden due to author-created content, with two notes clarifying configurable interfaces and user-opened content.
